purpose: Three independent workloads: workers contending for one mutex that is held across a sleep, a producer-consumer handoff on an unbuffered channel, and a CPU spin; CPU, block and mutex profiles each tell a different story.

representativeFlow.name: contended counter
representativeFlow.why: The mutex story crosses worker goroutines, Store.Add and the lock.

steps.role: runs Contend, Handoff and spin once and prints the results
starts workers goroutines that each call Store.Add perWorker times and waits on a WaitGroup
holds the mutex across time.Sleep(100 microseconds) before incrementing a map entry

cpu.note: spin is about 84 percent of CPU samples; the lock and channel waits cost almost no CPU

block.note: the top flat frame runtime.chanrecv1 is the testing framework (testing.(*B).doBench) waiting for the benchmark goroutine, not application code; application waits are Mutex.Lock under Store.Add, chanrecv2 in Handoff and WaitGroup.Wait in Contend

mutex.note: all mutex delay is attributed to the Unlock inside Store.Add; the stack is that of the code that held the lock

expectedFacts.statement: The only mutex in the program is Store.mu; contention comes from Store.Add holding it across time.Sleep(100 microseconds), so concurrent workers queue behind each other.
The mutex profile attributes all contention delay to Store.Add (reported at sync.(*Mutex).Unlock, the critical-section end) reached from Contend's worker goroutines.

The block profile covers every blocking wait, not only mutexes: Mutex.Lock under Store.Add, channel receive in Handoff (chanrecv2), WaitGroup.Wait in Contend and testing-framework waits (chanrecv1 from testing.(*B).doBench), the largest by delay.

Block and mutex profiles have sample types contentions (count) and delay (nanoseconds, shown as seconds by pprof); they measure time goroutines spent waiting, not CPU time. The CPU profile measures on-CPU time in nanoseconds of samples.
The CPU profile is dominated by spin; sleeping and blocked goroutines consume almost no CPU, so the CPU profile hides both the lock queue and the channel wait.
Handoff's consumer waits on the unbuffered channel because the producer sleeps 2 ms before each send; this is waiting time, not contention on a lock.

traps.statement: Reporting runtime.chanrecv1 under testing.(*B).doBench as an application bottleneck is wrong.
Describing block or mutex delay as CPU time is wrong.
Treating the block and mutex profiles as interchangeable is wrong; block includes channel and WaitGroup waits.
